core_obligations: Choose representatives (proof lines 3699-3710): by the construction of the derived pullback in this chapter, the author replaces the two complexes by K-flat resolutions with flat terms, on which Lf^* is computed by the naive pullback.

Compare the two sides (proof lines 3710-3720): with those representatives both sides are computed by the total complex of the pullbacks of the two complexes, using that the naive pullback commutes with the tensor product and with the total complex construction.

Conclude (proof lines 3720-3725): the identification for arbitrary complexes follows because the chosen representatives compute the derived functors, which gives the asserted bifunctorial isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Replace the complexes by K-flat resolutions with flat terms.
Compute both sides with the naive pullback and the total complex construction.
Identify them and conclude for arbitrary complexes.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the derived pullback is monoidal: Lf^* commutes with the derived tensor product up to a canonical bifunctorial isomorphism (statement lines 3683-3697). The proof uses the description of Lf^* on K-flat complexes with flat terms to replace the two complexes by such resolutions (proof lines 3699-3710), computes both sides with the naive pullback, which commutes with tensor products and total complexes (proof lines 3710-3720), and concludes for arbitrary complexes from the choice of representatives (proof lines 3720-3725). The non-formal content is the reduction to representatives on which both sides are naive. The claim is H2: one reduction plus one comparison of complexes.
